claim: Zebrafish lefty mutants exhibit excess Nodal signaling and increased specification of mesendoderm, resulting in embryonic lethality.
source: We find that zebrafish lefty mutants exhibit excess Nodal signaling and increased specification of mesendoderm, resulting in embryonic lethality.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in figures throughout the manuscript.

claim: Lethal patterning defects in lefty mutants can be rescued by ectopic expression of lefty far from its normal expression domain.
source: Lethal patterning defects in lefty mutants can be rescued by ectopic expression of lefty far from its normal expression domain or by spatially and temporally uniform exposure to a Nodal inhibitor drug.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 5 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Lethal patterning defects in lefty mutants can be rescued by spatially and temporally uniform exposure to a Nodal inhibitor drug.
source: Lethal patterning defects in lefty mutants can be rescued by ectopic expression of lefty far from its normal expression domain or by spatially and temporally uniform exposure to a Nodal inhibitor drug.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 6 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Drug-treated lefty mutants are less tolerant of mild perturbations to Nodal signaling levels than wild type embryos.
source: While drug-treated mutants are less tolerant of mild perturbations to Nodal signaling levels than wild type embryos, they can develop into healthy adults.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 8.

claim: Drug-treated lefty mutants can develop into healthy adults.
source: While drug-treated mutants are less tolerant of mild perturbations to Nodal signaling levels than wild type embryos, they can develop into healthy adults.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is demonstrated in Figure 6 showing adult fish.

claim: Patterning without inhibitory feedback is functional but fragile.
source: These results indicate that patterning without inhibitory feedback is functional but fragile.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the experimental findings.

claim: Feedback inhibition is a common feature of developmental pathways across phyla.
source: Feedback inhibition is a common feature of developmental pathways across phyla (Freeman, 2000; Freeman and Gurdon, 2002; Meinhardt, 2009; Piddini and Vincent, 2009; Ribes and Briscoe, 2009; Rogers and Schier, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Feedback inhibitors contribute to patterning processes in tissues ranging from the mouse neural tube and the zebrafish hindbrain, to the Drosophila wing and eye.
source: Feedback inhibitors contribute to patterning processes in tissues ranging from the mouse neural tube (Ribes and Briscoe, 2009) and the zebrafish hindbrain (White and Schilling, 2008), to the Drosophila wing (Gerlitz and Basler, 2002; Piddini and Vincent, 2009; Zeng et al., 2000) and eye (Freeman, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Inactivation of feedback inhibitors often results in disastrous patterning defects.
source: Consistent with a general requirement for feedback control in development, inactivation of feedback inhibitors often results in disastrous patterning defects.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Inhibitory feedback has been suggested to turn off pathway activity when it is no longer needed.
source: Inhibitory feedback has been suggested to turn off pathway activity when it is no longer needed, and to regulate spatial profiles of pathway activation (Barkai and Shilo, 2009; Ben-Zvi et al., 2008; Dessaud et al., 2007; Freeman, 2000; Gerlitz and Basler, 2002; Golembo et al., 1996; Lecuit and Cohen, 1998; Piddini and Vincent, 2009; Ribes and Briscoe, 2009; Schilling et al., 2012; Shiratori and Hamada, 2006; van Boxtel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Inhibitory feedback has been suggested to regulate spatial profiles of pathway activation.
source: Inhibitory feedback has been suggested to turn off pathway activity when it is no longer needed, and to regulate spatial profiles of pathway activation (Barkai and Shilo, 2009; Ben-Zvi et al., 2008; Dessaud et al., 2007; Freeman, 2000; Gerlitz and Basler, 2002; Golembo et al., 1996; Lecuit and Cohen, 1998; Piddini and Vincent, 2009; Ribes and Briscoe, 2009; Schilling et al., 2012; Shiratori and Hamada, 2006; van Boxtel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Negative feedback could enable the embryo to adjust signaling levels in response to unexpected perturbations or biochemical fluctuations.
source: Additionally, theoretical considerations suggest that negative feedback could enable the embryo to adjust signaling levels in response to unexpected perturbations or biochemical fluctuations (Barkai and Shilo, 2009; Eldar et al., 2003; Lander et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to theoretical studies.

claim: The Nodal/Lefty system has become a paradigm for feedback inhibition in development.
source: The Nodal/Lefty system has become a paradigm for feedback inhibition in development (Chen and Schier, 2002; Duboc et al., 2008; Freeman, 2000; Hamada, 2012; Kondo and Miura, 2010; Meinhardt, 2009; Meno et al., 1999; Nakamura et al., 2006; Rogers and Schier, 2011; Schier, 2009; Shen, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Nodal is a TGFβ superfamily ligand that induces the phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear localization of the transcription factor Smad2 in target cells.
source: Nodal is a TGFβ superfamily ligand that induces the phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear localization of the transcription factor Smad2 in target cells.
evidence: This statement describes established knowledge about Nodal signaling.

claim: In early embryos, Nodal signaling induces mesendodermal fates through graded activation of target genes, with higher signaling intensities biasing cells toward endoderm.
source: In early embryos, Nodal signaling induces mesendodermal fates through graded activation of target genes, with higher signaling intensities biasing cells toward endoderm.
evidence: This statement describes established knowledge about Nodal signaling.

claim: Leftys are secreted signaling inhibitors that prevent Nodal from binding to its receptors.
source: Nodal signaling intensity is shaped by the interplay between Nodal ligands and Leftys, secreted signaling inhibitors that prevent Nodal from binding to its receptors (Chen and Shen, 2004; Cheng et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss of Lefty inhibition results in expanded domains of Nodal target expression, increased mesendodermal specification, and embryonic lethality.
source: Studies of mouse lefty mutants and zebrafish lefty morphants reveal that loss of inhibition results in expanded domains of Nodal target expression, increased mesendodermal specification, and embryonic lethality (Agathon et al., 2001; Chen and Schier, 2002; Feldman et al., 2002; Meno et al., 1999; van Boxtel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Lefty production is coupled to Nodal signaling, forming a negative feedback loop that is conserved from sea urchins to humans.
source: Lefty production is coupled to Nodal signaling, forming a negative feedback loop that is conserved from sea urchins to humans.
evidence: This statement describes established knowledge about the Nodal/Lefty system.

claim: In zebrafish, lefty1 and lefty2 are induced by endogenous Nodal signaling at the blastoderm margin.
source: For example, in zebrafish, lefty1 and lefty2 are induced by endogenous Nodal signaling at the blastoderm margin, expression of Nodal can drive ectopic lefty production, and loss of Nodal signaling abolishes expression of lefty (Figure 1A,B) (Meno et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1A,B.

claim: Expression of Nodal can drive ectopic lefty production in zebrafish.
source: For example, in zebrafish, lefty1 and lefty2 are induced by endogenous Nodal signaling at the blastoderm margin, expression of Nodal can drive ectopic lefty production, and loss of Nodal signaling abolishes expression of lefty (Figure 1A,B) (Meno et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1A,B.

claim: Loss of Nodal signaling abolishes expression of lefty in zebrafish.
source: For example, in zebrafish, lefty1 and lefty2 are induced by endogenous Nodal signaling at the blastoderm margin, expression of Nodal can drive ectopic lefty production, and loss of Nodal signaling abolishes expression of lefty (Figure 1A,B) (Meno et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1A,B.

claim: The lefty1a145 allele contains a 13-base-pair deletion that removes the translational start site and part of the signal sequence.
source: lefty1a145 contains a 13-base-pair deletion that removes the translational start site and part of the predicted signal sequence (Figure 1C)
evidence: This statement describes the genetic mutation created in this study, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The lefty2a146 allele contains an 11-base-pair deletion that results in a stop codon after amino acid 18.
source: lefty2a146 contains an 11-base-pair deletion that results in a stop codon after amino acid 18 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement describes the genetic mutation created in this study, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutant lefty mRNAs were unable to induce Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes when injected into zebrafish embryos.
source: In contrast to wild type lefty mRNA, mutant lefty mRNAs were unable to induce Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes when injected into zebrafish embryos (Figure 1E–J").
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-J".

claim: lefty1-/- and lefty2-/- single mutants were viable and exhibited no or only minor increases in mesendodermal gene expression.
source: lefty1-/- and lefty2-/- single mutants were viable and exhibited no or only minor increases in mesendodermal gene expression (Figure 1N,O,T, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F)
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: lefty1-/- but not lefty2-/- mutants had heart laterality defects.
source: lefty1-/- but not lefty2-/- mutants had heart laterality defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Heart laterality defects are a hallmark of abnormal Nodal signaling.
source: lefty1-/- but not lefty2-/- mutants had heart laterality defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a hallmark of abnormal Nodal signaling (Bakkers et al., 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A single functional lefty allele was sufficient for viability.
source: A single functional lefty allele was sufficient for viability (Figure 1Q,R,T)
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Q,R,T.

claim: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- double mutants exhibited severe patterning defects, including loss of heart, eyes, and tail.
source: but lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- double mutants exhibited severe patterning defects, including loss of heart, eyes, and tail (Figure 1S, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant embryos had expanded pSmad2 signaling gradients prior to and during gastrulation.
source: At the level of tissue patterning, lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant embryos had expanded pSmad2 signaling gradients (Figure 2) prior to and during gastrulation
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Signaling gradients in lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants had higher amplitudes and longer ranges compared to wild type embryos.
source: Signaling gradients had higher amplitudes and longer ranges in double mutants compared to wild type embryos (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant embryos exhibited expanded expression of mesendodermal genes by gastrulation stages.
source: Consistent with the expansion of the pSmad2 signaling gradient, lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant embryos exhibited expanded expression of mesendodermal genes by gastrulation stages, whereas single mutants exhibited no or relatively minor upregulation (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants differ from lefty morphants in several aspects.
source: Expanded mesendoderm has also been reported in lefty double morphants (Agathon et al., 2001; Chen and Schier, 2002; Feldman et al., 2002; van Boxtel et al., 2015), but lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants differ in several aspects from morphants.
evidence: This statement is supported by comparison to prior literature and data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: lefty morphants display disrupted gastrulation and do not survive past 24 hr, whereas lefty double mutants successfully gastrulate and survive past 24 hr.
source: For example, lefty morphants display disrupted gastrulation and do not survive past 24 hr, whereas lefty double mutants successfully gastrulate and survive past 24 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Differences between lefty mutants and morphants are not caused by compensation in lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants but by off-target morpholino effects.
source: These differences are not caused by compensation in lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants but by off-target morpholino effects: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants injected with lefty1/2 morpholinos also display disrupted gastrulation and die by 24 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutations in the Nodal genes squint or cyclops suppressed multiple aspects of the lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant phenotype.
source: In support of this hypothesis, mutations in the Nodal genes squint or cyclops suppressed multiple aspects of the lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant phenotype (Figure 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: cyclops-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- and squint-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants formed eyes and full-length tails, structures missing in lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants.
source: cyclops-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- (Figure 4C'') and squint-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- (Figure 4F'') mutants formed eyes and full-length tails, structures missing in lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants (Figure 4A'', D'', M,N).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Upregulation of mesendodermal gene expression was suppressed in squint-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants compared to lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants.
source: Moreover, upregulation of mesendodermal gene expression was suppressed in squint-/-;lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants compared to lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants (Figure 4G–L''').
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Two functional nodal alleles are sufficient to generate mesendodermal gene expression patterns that are similar to those observed in wild type embryos with four nodal alleles and four lefty alleles.
source: Although these triple mutants are not viable, two functional nodal alleles are sufficient to generate mesendodermal gene expression patterns that are similar to those observed in wild type embryos with four nodal alleles and four lefty alleles.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Lefty inhibits both Squint and Cyclops.
source: In previous studies, removal of squint, but not cyclops, partially suppressed defects in lefty double morphants (Chen and Schier, 2002; Feldman et al., 2002), but our results indicate that Lefty inhibits both Squint and Cyclops.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 4, contrasting with prior literature.

claim: An ectopic, Nodal-independent source of Lefty at the animal pole can replace endogenous, Nodal-induced Lefty at the margin.
source: Strikingly, some of the lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutant hosts were rescued to normal morphology (Figure 5C–F', Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and developed into fertile adults (see Figure 5 legend for quantification). Thus, an ectopic, Nodal-independent source of Lefty at the animal pole can replace endogenous, Nodal-induced Lefty at the margin.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and related supplementary figures.

claim: The ability of ectopic Lefty-expressing clones to rescue lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants is consistent with the high diffusivity and long-range, extracellular distribution of Lefty protein.
source: The ability of ectopic Lefty-expressing clones to rescue lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants is consistent with the high diffusivity and long-range, extracellular distribution of Lefty protein (Chen and Schier, 2002; Marjoram and Wright, 2011; Müller et al., 2012) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The spatial coupling of lefty expression to Nodal signaling is not required for normal development.
source: In contrast to the requirement for spatially restricted Nodal signaling (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), the spatial coupling of lefty expression to Nodal signaling is not required for normal development.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 5 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Exposure of lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants to low concentrations of the Nodal inhibitor drug SB-505124 resulted in phenotypically normal embryos that developed into fertile adults.
source: Strikingly, exposure of lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants to inhibitor drug resulted in phenotypically normal embryos that developed into fertile adults (Figure 6B–I, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Different drug concentrations were required for rescue depending on the timing of treatment.
source: Different drug concentrations were required for rescue depending on the timing of treatment: Mutants exposed at earlier times were rescued by lower concentrations of Nodal inhibitor drug than mutants exposed at later times (Figure 6I, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Drug treatment starting hours before or after the onset of nodal and lefty expression rescued lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants.
source: Notably, even drug treatment starting hours before or after the onset of nodal and lefty expression rescued lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants (Figure 6D,F,I, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Highly specific timing or progressively increasing levels of inhibition during embryogenesis are not required for mesendoderm development.
source: These results show that highly specific timing or progressively increasing levels of inhibition during embryogenesis are not required for mesendoderm development.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants that were exposed to inhibitor before the onset of Nodal signaling initially displayed reduced Smad2 phosphorylation and endodermal gene expression compared to wild type.
source: Interestingly, despite their eventual rescue, lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants that were exposed to inhibitor before the onset of Nodal signaling not only showed reduced Smad2 phosphorylation compared to double mutants, but initially displayed reduced Smad2 phosphorylation and endodermal gene expression compared to wild type (Figure 6J–O'', Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The mechanism by which premature inhibitor exposure rescues development involves a delay in full activation of Nodal signaling.
source: The mechanism by which premature inhibitor exposure rescues development therefore involves a delay in full activation of Nodal signaling.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: lefty double mutants exposed to excess or sub-rescuing doses of inhibitor drug exhibited diminished or expanded pSmad2 activity gradients, respectively, with corresponding Nodal loss- or gain-of-function phenotypes.
source: Highlighting the sensitivity to Nodal inhibitor drug concentration, lefty double mutants exposed to excess or sub-rescuing doses exhibited diminished or expanded pSmad2 activity gradients, respectively, with corresponding Nodal loss- or gain-of-function phenotypes (Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced supplementary figures.

claim: Mutants exposed to inhibitor drug after the onset of Nodal signaling exhibited excess mesendodermal gene expression until ~5 hr post-exposure, but they ultimately developed normally.
source: Mutants exposed to inhibitor drug after the onset of Nodal signaling exhibited excess mesendodermal gene expression until ~5 hr post-exposure (Figure 6P–U'', Figure 6—figure supplement 3E,F), but they ultimately developed normally (Figure 6F,I, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The precise spatial and temporal coupling of lefty expression and Nodal activity is not essential for normal development.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that the precise spatial and temporal coupling of lefty expression and Nodal activity is not essential for normal development.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Injecting low levels of lefty1 mRNA into wild type embryos dramatically reduced lefty2 transcript abundance but left expression of the mesoderm marker noto relatively intact.
source: Injecting low levels of lefty1 mRNA into wild type embryos dramatically reduced lefty2 transcript abundance (Figure 7A,C,B,D), but left expression of the mesoderm marker noto relatively intact (Figure 7A', C', B', D').
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Increasing signaling by injecting mRNA encoding constitutively-active smad2 resulted in a marked increase in lefty2 expression but unchanged noto expression.
source: Conversely, increasing signaling by injecting mRNA encoding constitutively-active smad2 (CA-smad2, (Baker and Harland, 1996; Dick et al., 2000; Gritsman et al., 1999; Müller et al., 1999)) resulted in a marked increase in lefty2 expression (Figure 7E,G,F,H), but unchanged noto expression (Figure 7E', G', F' and H').
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Wild type embryos appear to compensate for perturbed Nodal signaling by sensitively adjusting lefty levels.
source: Wild type embryos thus appear to compensate for perturbed Nodal signaling by sensitively adjusting lefty levels.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Wild type embryos challenged with a small dose of lefty1 mRNA exhibited normal phenotypes at 24 hpf as well as normal mesendodermal gene expression at 50% epiboly and shield stages.
source: Wild type embryos challenged with a small dose of lefty1 mRNA exhibited normal phenotypes at 24 hpf (Figure 8A,B) as well as normal mesendodermal gene expression at 50% epiboly and shield stages (Figure 8H–I').
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Challenging feedback-compromised embryos with the same dose of lefty1 mRNA led to markedly decreased noto expression and 24 hpf phenotypes resembling partial loss-of-function Nodal mutants.
source: In contrast, challenging feedback-compromised embryos with the same dose of lefty1 mRNA led to markedly decreased noto expression (Figure 8I,K,M,I', K', M'), and 24 hpf phenotypes resembling partial loss-of-function Nodal mutants (Figure 8D,E) (Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Lefty-mediated inhibitory feedback can mitigate aberrant fluctuations in Nodal signaling levels.
source: These results reveal that Lefty-mediated inhibitory feedback can mitigate aberrant fluctuations in Nodal signaling levels (Figure 8G).
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Inhibitory feedback in the Nodal/Lefty system stabilizes Nodal signaling but is not essential for mesendoderm patterning and viability.
source: The results in this study show that inhibitory feedback in the Nodal/Lefty system stabilizes Nodal signaling but is not essential for mesendoderm patterning and viability.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, synthesizing all experimental findings.

claim: The rescue of lefty mutants by ectopic lefty expression and exposure to Nodal inhibitor drug is consistent with the high diffusivity of Lefty measured previously.
source: The rescue of lefty mutants by ectopic lefty expression (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2) and exposure to Nodal inhibitor drug (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1–4, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) is consistent with the high diffusivity of Lefty measured previously (Müller et al., 2012)
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data and citation to prior literature.

claim: Nodal signaling is already increased in lefty double mutants by sphere stage.
source: However, we find that Nodal signaling is already increased in lefty double mutants by sphere stage, suggesting an earlier role for Lefty (Figure 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mesendoderm patterning can proceed without progressively increasing inhibition and without temporally precise feedback inhibition.
source: Moreover, Lefty can be replaced by an inhibitor drug added as early as the 8 cell stage (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1–4, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), demonstrating that mesendoderm patterning can proceed without progressively increasing inhibition and without temporally precise feedback inhibition.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In drug-rescued lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants, Nodal activity gradients and mesendodermal gene expression patterns initially differed from wild type.
source: In drug-rescued lefty1-/-;lefty2-/- mutants, Nodal activity gradients and mesendodermal gene expression patterns initially differed from wild type (Figure 6J–U'', Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 6—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Precise wild type activity gradients and mesendodermal gene expression patterns during early embryogenesis are not essential for germ layer development.
source: However, rescued mutants developed into fertile adults (Figure 6H, Figure 6—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that precise wild type activity gradients and mesendodermal gene expression patterns during early embryogenesis are not essential for germ layer development.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: The dispensability of inhibitory feedback in the Nodal/Lefty system raises questions about the role of Nodal and Lefty as an activator/inhibitor pair in self-organizing reaction-diffusion models.
source: Third, the dispensability of inhibitory feedback in the Nodal/Lefty system raises questions about the role of Nodal and Lefty as an activator/inhibitor pair in self-organizing reaction-diffusion models.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: Nodal and Lefty fulfill the key regulatory and biophysical requirements of a short-to-mid-range autocatalytic activator and a long-range feedback inhibitor.
source: Although Nodal and Lefty fulfill the key regulatory and biophysical requirements of a short-to-mid-range autocatalytic activator and a long-range feedback inhibitor (Hamada, 2012; Meno et al., 1999; Müller et al., 2012; Schier, 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Development can be normal without inhibitory feedback in the Nodal/Lefty system, indicating that this system does not require the ability to form self-organizing reaction-diffusion patterns.
source: our finding that development can be normal without inhibitory feedback indicates that this system does not require the ability to form self-organizing reaction-diffusion patterns.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: The pre-patterning of the early embryo by maternal factors and the local activation of Nodal may eliminate the need for self-organizing pattern generation by the Nodal/Lefty circuit.
source: Instead, it is conceivable that the pre-patterning of the early embryo by maternal factors and the local activation of Nodal eliminate the need for self-organizing pattern generation by the Nodal/Lefty circuit.
evidence: This statement is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Nodal and Lefty may have constituted a reaction-diffusion activator/inhibitor pair in ancestral organisms but, through the addition of other regulatory layers, mesendoderm patterning lost the requirement for inhibitory feedback.
source: In this scenario, Nodal and Lefty may have constituted a reaction-diffusion activator/inhibitor pair in ancestral organisms but, through the addition of other regulatory layers, mesendoderm patterning lost the requirement for inhibitory feedback.
evidence: This statement is speculation about evolutionary history.

claim: Feedback may be required to optimize inhibitor levels, as suggested by the narrow range (~2 fold) of inhibitor concentrations that rescue Lefty loss.
source: Feedback may be required to optimize inhibitor levels, as suggested by the narrow range (~2 fold) of inhibitor concentrations that rescue Lefty loss (Figure 6I, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: The adjustment of lefty expression in response to slight alterations in Nodal signaling and the failure of feedback-decoupled embryos to cope with perturbations in Nodal signaling support the idea that feedback buffers fluctuations in pathway activity.
source: Indeed, the adjustment of lefty expression in response to slight alterations in Nodal signaling (Figure 7) and the failure of feedback-decoupled embryos to cope with perturbations in Nodal signaling (Figure 8) support this idea.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: The ability to dynamically adjust pathway activity may allow the embryo to create reliable patterns in the face of endogenous signaling fluctuations and uncertain environmental conditions.
source: The ability to dynamically adjust pathway activity may allow the embryo to create reliable patterns in the face of endogenous signaling fluctuations and uncertain environmental conditions.
evidence: This statement is speculation about the function of feedback.

claim: Lefty feedback does not protect the embryo against all perturbations: Drug-rescued lefty mutants actually fared better than wild type embryos when challenged with injection of squint mRNA.
source: We note, however, that Lefty feedback does not protect the embryo against all perturbations: Drug-rescued lefty mutants actually fared better than wild type embryos when challenged with injection of squint mRNA (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Embryos bearing compromised patterning circuits could be identified by sequencing a single embryonic cell, and birth defects could be prevented by exposure to the appropriate small molecule.
source: Although suggested applications to human embryos might currently seem fanciful and would be challenging and fraught with ethical concerns, embryos bearing compromised patterning circuits could be identified by sequencing a single embryonic cell, and birth defects could be prevented by exposure to the appropriate small molecule.
evidence: This statement is speculation about potential future applications.

claim: A tethered form of Wingless can replace endogenous Wingless, challenging models in which a gradient of diffusing Wingless is indispensable for tissue patterning.
source: For example, a tethered form of Wingless can replace endogenous Wingless, challenging models in which a gradient of diffusing Wingless is indispensable for tissue patterning (Alexandre et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The observations challenge models in which inhibitory feedback is an absolute requirement for patterning and viability, but support the idea that inhibitory feedback enhances robustness by stabilizing signaling during development.
source: In the same vein, our observations challenge models in which inhibitory feedback is an absolute requirement for patterning and viability, but support the idea that inhibitory feedback enhances robustness by stabilizing signaling during development.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: Mutations in lefty genes were induced using TALENs.
source: Mutations in lefty genes were induced using TALENs (Bedell et al., 2012; Sander et al., 2011; Sanjana et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement describes the methods used in the study.

claim: The lefty1 TALEN pair was generated using the FLASH assembly kit.
source: The lefty1 TALEN pair was generated using the FLASH assembly kit (Reyon et al., 2012)
evidence: This statement describes the methods used in the study.

claim: The lefty2 TALEN pair was generated using the TALE Toolbox.
source: the lefty2 TALEN pair was generated using the TALE Toolbox (Sanjana et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement describes the methods used in the study.

claim: The 13-base-pair deletion in lefty1a145 destroys a PshAI restriction site.
source: The 13-base-pair deletion in lefty1a145 destroys a PshAI restriction site.
evidence: This statement describes the methods used for genotyping.

claim: The Nodal inhibitor SB-505124 selectively inhibits Nodal signaling by preventing ATP from binding to Nodal receptors.
source: To test whether patterning can occur when Nodal pathway inhibition is spatially and temporally decoupled from Nodal activity, we attempted to replace the inhibitory activity of Lefty with a small molecule drug, SB-505124, that selectively inhibits Nodal signaling by preventing ATP from binding to Nodal receptors (Figure 6A) (DaCosta Byfield et al., 2004; Fan et al., 2007; Hagos and Dougan, 2007; Hagos et al., 2007; van Boxtel et al., 2015; Vogt et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.
